articleTitle: Analysis of Average Symbol Error Probability of MDPSK, MFSK and MPSK in the Beaulieu-Xie Fading
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: In this paper, closed-form expressions for average symbol error probability (ASEP) of M-ary differential phase-shift keying (MDPSK), non-coherent M-ary frequency-shift keying (MFSK), and coherent M-ary phase-shift keying (MPSK) over the Beaulieu-Xie fading channel are derived. The Beaulieu-Xie fading channel was proposed by Beaulieu and Jiandong to analyze the conditions of wireless environments in which the received power consists of multiple-specular components with some diffuse power e.g. high speed trains and femtocells. In this paper, no approximation has been used to derive the ASEP. The results demonstrated in this paper are supposed to give important and useful information to evaluate the performance of fading channels. The verification of analytical results is done by comparing them with Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: A Survey on Energy Harvesting Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Drastic development in the wireless communication systems is leading to the issue of spectrum scarcity and to resolve this issue, cognitive radio (CR) is emerging as one of the most capable solution. Energy harvesting phenomenon in cognitive radio networks (EH-CRNs) makes these communication systems an energy efficient one. This paper reviews the different energy harvesting techniques in CRNs, existing work on EH-CRNs and future research directions in EH-CRNs. Different energy harvesting sources for CRNs are discussed and depending upon the power storage potential of the EH-CRNs, two types of harvesting models that is harvest-use model and harvest-store-use model are explained. The existing work on EH-CRNs which includes resource allocation, throughput maximization and secure information transfer with both linear as well as non-linear energy harvesting models is discussed. Finally, future research directions in energy harvesting cognitive radios are discussed briefly.

articleTitle: Detection of Cervical Cancer using GLCM and Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Early detection of cancer can lead to a higher likelihood of survival, lower costs of care which would further result in lowering death rates and disability due to cancer. Introduced in March 1924, colposcopy was used to detect the cause of abnormal looking cervix and hence provide appropriate treatment. Being prone to human errors, colposcopy can lead to misleading results for detection of cervical cancer. This paper aims at presenting a convenient and automated method of detection of cervical cancer and classifying images as cancerous or non-cancerous. After applying scaling on the images obtained via colposcopy, the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) was constructed. The Haralick features extracted from the above-constructed matrix were hence used to classify images into cancerous and non-cancerous using Support Vector Machines (SVM).

articleTitle: ReachOut Smart Safety Device
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Today, the safety of women and children has become the preeminent issue of our society. The number of incidents and victims is rising with each passing day. This paper proposes a model which will help ensure the safety of women and children. Since the person in danger will not be able to respond competently in critical situations, the need for an emergency device which easily takes input in case of emergency is the primary motive behind this paper. This paper proposes to build a prototype that can be easily carried and worn, that takes input from distress button and sends the fetched location on the cloud and notifies the respective parents regarding the same. The wearable device will have a GPS module for fetching the coordinates after the panic button is pressed. The device works with Raspberry Pi for running the GPS and updating the cloud database. The android application with the parents will fetch the stored coordinates from the cloud when they receive an emergency notification. This action allows the emergency contacts to view the most recent location of the person in trouble. The application gives the address, map location and routes of the person who needs help.

articleTitle: Atlas Simulation of a Long-Infrared P+-N Homojunction Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: This paper presents the Atlas simulation of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-n homojunction photodiode based on Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x=0.22</sub>Te semiconductor material for operation in the long-infrared (LIR) spectral region (2-12 μm). The simulated photodiode has been studied at 77 and 300 K in terms of the various electro-optical parameters for example energy bandgap diagram, the electric field profile, the current densities, external quantum efficiency (QE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ext</sub>), and noise equivalent power (NEP) with respect to applied bias voltage, device thickness, and operating wavelength. The simulated 2D and 3D results are comparable with the results obtained from analytical equations based on drift-diffusion, tunneling and Chu's approximation techniques. The photodiode exhibits high electric field, low value of zero bias dark current density of 0.26 pA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, better photocurrent density of 4.9 μA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 3-dB bandwidth of 104 GHz, high external quantum efficiency of 58.34% and low noise equivalent power of 2.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> W.

articleTitle: FPGA Based Solution For Ethernet Controller As Alternative For TCP/UDP Software Stack
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: This paper presents an Ethernet based embedded system solution by interfacing FPGA with W5500 for implementation of UDP/IP stack. Ethernet based embedded system is required in variety of applications for transmitting high speed data over long distances. FPGA is a potent solution for developing customized Ethernet based embedded system. FPGA based ethernet solution either utilizes high cost commercially available IP cores or requires TCP/IP core development with high level of HDL expertise. Commercially available external ethernet controller like W5500 chip with inbuilt TCP/IP protocol offers simple, low cost and higher data rate transmission with FPGA based solution for embedded systems. This approach reduces coding complexity and the development cost and time. This design was implemented in XC7Z020 FPGA device and evaluated for data transmission rate up to 32 MBPS for data packet size of 1 KB using UDP Protocol using W5500 external ethernet controller.

articleTitle: Analysis of Varied Dielectrics as Surface Passivation on AlGaN/GaN HEMT for Analog Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: In this work, AlGaN/GaN HEMT device performance for different dielectrics as surface passivation have been studied. Due to the high thermal stability, high dielectric constant and high reliability of HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> but limiting interface quality, a stack of silicon nitride with hafnium dioxide has been proposed as surface passivation material for AlGaN/GaN HEMT, attributed to the good interface of Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with GaN. The device performance of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with various dielectrics i.e. SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and a stack of Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as surface passivation layer (SPL) have also been compared using device simulator. Evaluated electrical parameters show that the device passivated with a stack of Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> shows high drain current, high breakdown voltage, higher gain as well as higher current switching ratio in comparison with other dielectric materials used as surface passivation, thus the results indicate that the AlGaN/GaN HEMT with stack (Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) surface passivation has better device performance suitable for high-power applications.

articleTitle: A Survey on FPGA Implementations in Embedded Augmented Reality Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Since a long ago, most of the Augmented Reality (AR) applications are built using some general purpose devices such as computers and handhelds. In such general purpose devices, tasks are being processed using different softwares that make it difficult to obtain the real time results with high resolution and frame rate. There is a need to maintain a good performance but it invariably results into high cost of the overall project due to the requirement of higher clock frequency and high power. Mobility and processing power are the two basic requirements of an augmented reality application to provide an efficient immersion to the end user. An embedded architecture developed on Field Programmable Gate Array Logic (FPGA) can supply both mobility and processing power to the AR applications. FPGA is a tiny chip that has the efficiency of hardware level executions. This paper gives a detailed account of FPGAs in AR applications in the field of computer vision & image processing, multimedia & computer graphics, communication and wearable computing.

articleTitle: A Novel Zero Cross-correlation Diagonal Identity Matrix Code
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Optical Code Division Multiple Access system (OCDMA) is an imminent technology to expunge the limitations of ever increasing data traffic and multiple user access in optical networks. However Multiple Access Interference (MAI) and cross correlation among different codes are prominent issues of SAC OCDMA systems. In order to eliminate cross correlation and to suppress MAI, in this work, we proposed novel Zero cross-correlation (ZCC) Diagonal Identity Matrices codes (DIM). Further, comparison of DIM code is carried out with Enhanced Double weight Codes (EDW) in similar environment in terms of Bit error rate, extinction ratio, Q factor, signal to noise ratio, eye height etc. Codes are investigated at the speed on 30 Gbps and total simultaneous users considered are seven. Mapping free technique is used for both OCDMA SAC-codes which permits service provider to design codes for large no. of users. Proposed novel SAC-OCDMA diagonal identity matrix codes have advantage that it can be designed for any number of users. It is perceived that due to zero cross correlation DIM codes exhibits better performance than EDW codes.

Author Keywords: Optical Code Division Multiple Access system (OCDMA)

articleTitle: Ultra-thin and Dual Band Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: In this paper, we simulate the polarization dependent metamaterial absorber (MMA) based on split ring-dish (SRD) structure. The results have been compared with dish (D) and ring-dish (RD) based structure in THz range. The dish based MMA structure demonstrates the perfect absorption at 5.4 THz, whereas ring-dish based MMA exhibits two peaks at 2.7 and 5.6 THz. Further, by splitting the ring (named as split ring-dish), absorption peak at 2.7 THz is shifted to 4.2 THz. The surface current and electric field distribution have been measured to provide further understanding of absorptivity. The resonating frequency of the SRD-MMA has been tuned with change in incident and polarization angle.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed UWB Reconfigurable Antenna (RF MEMS Switch) with X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Hexagonal Shape radiating patch with reconfigurable characteristics for WiMAX/C/WLAN band is presented which is simulated on RT Duroid5880 substrate and is fed by CPW. Fractional bandwidth of antenna corresponds to 153.62% with high rejection dual band-notch reconfigurable characteristics excluding interfering bands WiMAX (3.30GHz–3.80GHz)/C-Band (3.80GHz–4.20GHz)/WLAN (IEEE802.11a/h/j/n5.15GHz–5.35GHz, 5.25GHz–5.35GHz, 5.47GHz–5.725GHz,5.725GHz–5.825GHz) using radio frequency micro electro mechanical systems (RF MEMS) shunt switch. The proposed antenna exhibits 3.4dBi–6.32dBi gain and 78–94% radiation efficiency. The group delay ≤1.0ns is also maintained in the entire operating band. Good dipole like radiation pattern in E-plane and omni-directional pattern in H-plane is also well maintained in the operating band with less co polarization with compact dimensions of 20 × 22 × 0.782 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Myoelectric Signal Based Multiple Grip Pattern Prosthetic Arm
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: In today's time there are a lot of skilled people who cannot work due to the loss of limb. These people are known as arm amputees. They need help of someone even to perform their mundane task. In other words they are capable to perform a task yet not self-sufficient due to their disability. This paper aims to provide a feasible solution to the amputee patients. Even though the patient has lost his/her limb, the muscles are still functioning near the amputated part. This projects focuses on the electromyography signals generated by the user near the amputated part. These ultra low level signals are picked up by the EMG sensor, the noise is filtered and important features are extracted out of it. A fuzzy logic system is created for various grip patterns on the LabVIEW software using the extracted features. The Arduino controller is then instructed to actuate the servo motors as per the grip pattern output from the LabVIEW. The servo motors in turn is used to actuate the fingers of the prosthetic arm via fishing lines as tendons. The prosthetic arm is 3D printed using ABS plastic to reduce the weight of the overall system and to reduce the cost factor. In this way different gripping patterns is controlled on the prosthetic arm based on the features extracted. The versatility of this project lies in distinguishing the EMG signals depending on the intensity of the signal, thus performing various gripping patterns on the prosthetic arm.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Performance of Underwater Free Space Optical Link in the Presence of Air Bubbles
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Free space optics (FSO) has become a potential candidate for underwater communications due to its tremendous advantages such as large bandwidth, security and high data rates than that of acoustic and radio waves at moderate distances. When an optical beam interacts with water molecules, it suffers from absorption, scattering and attenuation phenomenon that further results into the poor reception of the signal. The suspended particulate matter such as air bubbles severely degrade the system performance. The air bubbles in water spread the optical beam into spatial and temporal domain, distort the signal amplitude and hence deviate the optical beam from the desired path. So, an underwater FSO link was established to study its performance in the presence of different sized air bubbles. The attenuation constant, relative intensity with respect to forward scattering angle and randomness caused by this impairment have been evaluated experimentally. The attenuation constant rises in the presence of air bubble populations and relative intensity tends to decrease with increasing forward scattering angles. Further the increase in randomness of received intensity is evaluated and compared for two different bubble populations.

articleTitle: Bluetooth Enabled Anti-Theft System Using Android Based Handheld Device
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Vehicle theft count comprises a major portion of the total incidents of crime today. The researchers and vehicle manufacturers throughout the world have been working on various theories to come up with a device that helps to curb this menace. The existing systems are beyond the limit of masses and thousands of vehicles are still being stolen daily. The Bluetooth-enabled cost-effective solution has been made to protect the vehicles. This paper attempts to utilize two physically disjoint units in conjunction with each other, an intention to provide a fool-proof mechanism against vehicle theft. A prototype was made using arduino, fingerprint sensor and Bluetooth. Android smart phones are being used to design for the user interface that allows access of the vehicle to an intended person only.

articleTitle: Power Efficient Arithmetic and Logical Unit Design on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is one of the most crucial part of all the digital circuits that is used to perform arithmetic and logical operations. An energy and power efficient ALU is designed in this paper by employing different energy and power efficient techniques. ALU is designed on ISE project navigator of Xilinx software and power analysis is done on X Power Analyzer. Two energy efficient techniques named as Frequency scaling and Input/Output (I/O) standard scaling are employed on ALU. In the frequency scaling technique, frequency range of the design is varied from Mega Hertz (MHz) to Tera Hertz (THz) and power analysis is done to figure out the most efficient frequency in terms of power consumption. Power analysis is also done at different I/O standards of Low Voltage Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (LVCMOS) logic family to find out the most power efficient IO standard. The device is operated on ARTIX-7 FPGA technology with a channel length of 28 nano meters (nm). It has been concluded from results that maximum power is being saved at LVCMOS 33 I/O standard at a frequency of 1MHz.

articleTitle: Nanostructure Materials For Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage: A Review
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Energy production from renewable sources is increasing at a quite high rate in order to have a refined phase of energy consumption. Hydrogen has emerged as a clean and efficient energy carrier since 1839. The storage of hydrogen is one of the essential requirements for the development of renewable-based energy system but, it still remains a great challenge for technologists. Many researchers have reported about the numerous materials being used for hydrogen storage. Nanostructure oxide and activated carbon (aC) material seem to be more suitable for storing the hydrogen efficiently. In the present review, numerous hydrogen storage materials those are being used for electrochemical hydrogen storage have been discussed. The relative comparison of different hydrogen storage materials may be very useful for future experiments as electrochemical hydrogen storage.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Uniformity of Illuminance in Indoor VLC System
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: White LEDs are becoming an attractive choice in indoor visible light communication (VLC) and the uniformity of illuminance is a critical issue in VLC systems. In this paper, we have evaluated the illumination uniformity for three different LED lamp arrangements with varying semi-angles of the transmitter in MATLAB. In all the arrangements, (3×3) LEDs are symmetrically placed on the ceiling in a square room. The first order reflections are taken into account for evaluating the performance of the proposed system. Next, we discussed about the power received at the receiving plane considering reflection from the walls. The simulation results show that there is significant improvement in uniformity with the increase in the semi-angle of the transmitter up to a certain distance limited by the walls of the room.

articleTitle: Compensation of Power Amplifier Non-linearity for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation and implementation of digital pre-distorter based linearizer for high power amplifier used in satellite communication systems. The digital pre-distorter technique discussed here is based on Look-up-Table (LUT) based approach which can be implemented in on-board digital processor. LUT content is derived from inverse polynomial model for memoryless RF power amplifiers. The performance of LUT based pre-distorter model has been verified using Kintex-7 FPGA platform and Ku-band 70W Travelling Wave Tube Amplifier (TWTA).

articleTitle: Design of Ku Band Reflectarray Antenna Using Novel Half Ellipse Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: This paper presents a 3×3 reflectarray (RA) antenna designed for Ku-Band Satellite Communication Applications. The unit element is a single layer structure and is linearly polarized. The purpose of this RA is to operate at 12.5GHz. The proposed RA displays high gain and good phase characteristics making it suitable to act as a reflector. Several structures of the unit-cells were designed and the best of them were used to construct the array. The array is excited using a source patch placed at a distance of 5λ/4.

articleTitle: Harmonic Minimization in Modified Multilevel Inverter For Hybrid Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Renewable energy sources play a significant role for uninterrupted power supply in remote places. The paper presents the concept of a micro-grid fed from renewable energy sources for both PV/wind with maximum power point tracking and cascaded H bridge multilevel inverter system. The entire system is grid connected. A modified design is carried out for 13-level multilevel inverter topology where it works at a high switching frequency to reduce the size and losses. An LCL filter and a STATCOM are connected for smoothing of the grid line voltage. The multilevel inverter gating signals are driven using Artificial Neural Network technique for performance improvement. The objective here is to calculate the total harmonic distortion of modified cascaded H bridge multilevel inverter to improve the power quality of grid connected systems. The entire model is implemented with the help of Simulink®MATLAB. The simulation results are analyzed, presented and compared.

Author Keywords: cascaded H bridge multilevel inverter CHBMLI

articleTitle: Exfoliation of Graphene Oxide via Chemical Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Reduced graphene oxide (RGO) is a potential material for new era nano devices due to its novel property and morphology. The numerous synthesis methods for this material have been explored by various researchers. The chemical method named modified hummer method used to oxidate the graphite to form graphene oxide (GO). Afterward, it is exfoliated and reduced to form reduced graphene oxide is the most relevant method. Hence, in the present paper, Reduced Graphene oxide (RGO) has been obtained by this method. In this paper, Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) is used as a reducing agent in chemical reduction of exfoliated GO. X-Ray diffraction (XRD) peaks are observed at 25.5° with interspacing distance 4.038 A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> and at 26.2° with an interspacing distance of 1.657 A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>, for the GO and RGO respectively. The scanning electron microscopy images GO and RGO predicts multi-layers morphology. The view of RGO reveals the exfoliated multi-layer confirms the appearance of transparent wrinkles and due to the reduction of the oxygen-containing functional group. The Raman spectroscopy of graphene oxide displays strong G and D peak at 1592 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 1358 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> respectively which attributes to local defects and disorders. Whereas for RGO has been shifted back to 1585 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 1340 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for G and D peak respectively. There is a rise in intensities ratio from 0.770 - 0.902 associated with decreased in average size of sp2 domains. So, RGO is considered as a smart material for different nano electronics applications like sensors, solar cells, optoelectronics devices, energy storage capacitors, lithium-ion batteries etc.

articleTitle: Development of Fiber Optic Sensors for Leak Detection in Underground Energy Storage Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: The performance monitoring of energy storage pipelines has been investigated using efficient optical strain sensors. Leakage and corrosion are major hazard that occur in underground energy storage pipelines due to cracks, drilling, geohazards and manufacturing defects. The experimental results report that the proposed sensor design achieved a wavelength shift of 3.2 nm with applied load of 65 kN resulting into strain of 2495με. Here, readings were acquired every 5 minutes to decrease measurement noise. The experimental strain outcomes are observed both for open (telephone and transmission pipelines) and closed pipelines (gasoline, liquid petroleum, chemicals, water, sewer lines, storm sewers) and it is examined that the proposed sensor can monitor strain and corrosion simultaneously.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of LNT (Li2O– Nb2O5–TiO2) Based Dielectric Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: The present paper reports the synthesis, structural and dielectric properties of the M-phase solid solutions in the Li2O-Nb2O5-TiO2 (LNT) system. M-phase LNT ceramic powders have been successfully synthesized by solid state reaction method at 1100° C. Structural analysis of sintered samples has been carried out by using the measurement of X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) and High resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM). The dielectric analysis of the LNT ceramics have also been studied. These materials are suitable candidate for resonators, filters, antenna etc. for the emerging wireless communications applications.

articleTitle: Combinational Logic Optimization for Ultra-Constrained Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Modern computing paradigm such as the Internet of Things demands edge devices with limited resources to be capable of complex computing functions. In this work, we discuss a relatively new approach to combinational circuit optimization based on a low multiplicative complexity heuristic. The purpose of the optimization heuristic is to produce low gate count circuit to enable complex transformation to fit in devices that operate in ultra-constrained environments. We explain the concepts behind the heuristic and review the original optimization algorithm based on the heuristic. A new approach is then proposed to eliminate reliance on randomness in the original algorithm to improve computational time and quality of results.

articleTitle: Investigation of Grating Parameters Impact on Spectral Characteristics of LPFG using Two-Layer Fiber Geometry
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: The study on spectral characteristics of long period fiber grating (LPFG) explores its usefulness in many applications. This scenario insists the researchers to calculate the impact of LPFG's parameters on its characteristics. The paper presents the effect of grating length and grating period on the spectral characteristics of LPFG. Their impact is calculated in terms of variation in position of resonant wavelength and attenuation band depth. For this, the transmission profiles of LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub> and LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">05</sub> cladding modes are kept under observation here. The spectral profiles are calculated using analytical expressions obtained through coupled mode theory. The two layer fiber geometrical model is implemented on SMF28 optical fiber parameters to evaluate propagation constants of fiber's core region's and cladding region's modes. The results show linear increase in attenuation depth of spectrum with increase in grating length. On the other hand, with the rise in periodicity the shift in resonant wavelength is towards longer wavelengths.

articleTitle: Photonic Based Refractive Index Sensor for Portlandite Monitoring in Civil Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: In this paper, photonic based refractive index sensor is proposed to monitor portlandite in civil structures. Portlandite is oxide mineral that naturally occurs from calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and calcium analogue of brucite (Mg(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>). Portlandite creates a problem in concrete in terms of corrosion and spalling. The proposed sensor is designed to detect the presence of portlandite by measuring Ca(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Mg(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> chemicals. It is observed that the proposed sensor produces a wavelength shift of 0.008μm and 0.005μm for Ca(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Mg(OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> respectively.

articleTitle: Journey of UWB Antenna Towards Miniaturization for RF/Wireless Community
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: UWB (Ultra-Wideband) has stepped up its footprint in communication world with a lot of promising features. It includes high data-rate for short-range communication, huge bandwidth for large data transfer, good alternative for indoor navigation and finally high resolution imaging utilizing its robust feature to multipath fading. The antenna is one of the key building blocks in UWB wireless system. Being an electronic eye of the system, its design gets utmost importance as compared to its other constituent parts. Main challenge in this antenna design is to maintain the 10-dB return loss throughout the entire bandwidth of the desired frequency spectrum. This article starts with a brief introduction of particular design challenges of UWB antennas, followed by state-of-the-art solutions. Next, various miniaturization topologies are addressed. Planar designs have been emphasized here due to their unique cost effective features along with other merits, related to practical usage. This work also outlines about the extension of operating frequency bands than that of conventional ultra-wideband, recommended by FCC, USA in 2002. Further, this wide operating regime can be detrimental for already existed wireless appliances falling in this spectrum. Faithful techniques to mitigate the frequency interference problem are adopted here. Future application of this technology towards the medical imaging is also brought out in this work.

articleTitle: Home Automation Using Energy Usage
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Home automation is usually referred to the technique for controlling devices autonomously based on certain parameters. However, most of the system that exist is more of remote control rather than home automation. In this research paper, we're presenting a model for automating homes based on energy usage as the primary parameter. The autonomous control based on primary parameters are based on the application of machine learning using artificial neural network(s). The model is essentially a recommendation system and presents the user with alerts or recommendation. Remote control and monitoring act as the base of the system and two architecture(s) are presented to attain the same. The first is a distributed system where, multiple nodal points communicate with the global server independently. The second is a centralised system, where multiple nodal points communicate with a centralised local server and the server communicates with the central global server hosted over internet. The paper also discusses an advanced secured method for communication between the edge device and the server. As we are dealing with low power and low processing capability devices, security is a very big challenge. Here we have proposed an advanced multi-stage security-based system to provide maximum possible security in embedded platforms.

articleTitle: Provisioning Authentication On Demand in Wireless Sensor Networks: PAW
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Impersonation and node compromise are common attacks on wireless sensor networks. In these attacks, the attacker gains access to a node or pretends to be some legitimate node of the network, injects and modifies messages, putting the network security at stake. To combat these attacks, authentication mechanism can be employed to ensure that data is not altered during transit and its sourced from a legitimate node. Any wireless sensor network application without authentication but encompassing other security measures are incomplete and insignificant. The authentication techniques proposed for traditional computer networks are based on certificates - issued and validated by a third party and another method is based on symmetric key cryptography that requires very high communications. Due to resource constraints of the wireless sensor networks, the authentication should be light weight along with other security features such as scalability and reduced consumption of resources. In this paper, a new security service to thwart unauthorized access into the network through PAW: Provisioning authentication on demand in Wireless Sensor Networks scheme is proposed. The PAW scheme is relatively more secure than the existing schemes and has reduced communication overhead.

articleTitle: Passive Optical Network Evolution to Next Generation Passive Optical Network: A Review
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet traffic shoves the communication networks to optical access networks for enhancing the transmission information rate. Passive optical network (PON) is a developed and most encouraging access network which provides the high bandwidth, information rate and low cost architecture for home and business enterprises. The main aim of this paper is to review the standardization evolution of PON to next generation passive optical network (NG-PON). Additionally, the literature review of PON and NG-PON based technologies are discussed. Also, it presents the possible challenges in NG-PON alongside their strengths and weakness in different techniques.

articleTitle: Static Force Analysis of a Climbing Bot With Target Tracking Using WSNs
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: This paper describes the design process of a climbing bot -”Octo-Climber', which adopts SgI and has the potential to carry a material in a confined space. The main contribution of this paper is static force analysis. However, existing literature related to tracking problem mainly focused on distributed tracking of a single target. It is found that if Octo-Climber is able to successfully transit from a vertical plane to an overhead plane without sliding, it could transit between other planes as well. The proposed techniques are thoroughly investigated in a real indoor environment. In addition, several criteria for choosing relevant data for the positioning purposes have been explored. WSNs is utilized to illustrate the interactions between the robots and its corresponding targets, and represents the connection weight between the robots and targets. The sufficient conditions for both surface transition and static force analysis of the closed-loop system are derived. Finally, algorithms are developed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the main results.

articleTitle: Rate Adaptation in Generalised Spatial Modulation with RCPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2018 6th Edition of International Conference on Wireless Networks & Embedded Systems (WECON)
abstract: Link adaptation is crucial in the upcoming broadband wireless systems, where there are stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. It is well established in single antenna systems, whereas it is challenging and at the same time promising in Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) communication. Changing the modulation order/coding scheme or switching between MIMO modes for adaptation is rather complex and requires high adaptive control overhead. As an alternative, error control coding, which is widely used in MIMO can be modified to make the system rate adaptive, with or without constellation change. In this paper, we present an adaptive transmission technique in Generalised Spatial Modulation (GSM) MIMO using Rate Compatible Punctured Convolutional (RCPC) codes. An antenna grouping method based on limited channel state information (CSI) feedback is used here to select the puncturing matrices and the active antennas. The system throughput and BER performance are analyzed for various channel selection and puncturing schemes.
